name: Hollin
description: The Wardens' spare cob: a dun mare of fifteen hands with a hogged mane, a dorsal stripe and feathered heels, in the Wardens' green saddle cloth. Lent to the Foundling by Wren Tallow at Merrowby.

home.notes: tethered in the yard of the Toll's Lip, a few paces off its door

name: Nettle
description: Rosen Wyke's old forest pony: a grey-dun mare of thirteen hands, sure-footed on roots and scree, under a Woodfolk saddle-cloth of undyed wool. Rosen rode her as a girl and says she is too small for her now, which is not true.

look.notes: kin of the cob: the same forge body, smaller, greyer, with an undyed Woodfolk cloth

name: Forty
description: The Wicks' old cart-horse: a dark bay mare of sixteen hands with a white blaze and a draught horse's feathers, who pulled the eel-cart to Tollmere until the Tallymen priced Jory's barrow off Lantern Row. Jory named her the day of the fine. She has had nothing to pull since, and it has made her sour and very fond of apples.

look.notes: kin of the cob: the same forge body, bigger and darker, in a lake-blue Gullhithe cloth

home.notes: in the lee of the Wicks' cottage, with the empty cart-shafts
